## Branch state

- The branch is rebased on main as of this morning, with no conflicts.
- Commit `4f9e2a1` holds the refactor and commit `b07c3d9` the tests.
- Required CI fails at this head: the lint job reports 14 offenses in `importer/retry.rb` and `sync/worker.rb`, mostly line length and an unused variable left from the removed helper. The other required checks pass.
- The optional benchmark job was skipped by the pipeline, as it is on every branch.

## Notes

- The jitter now uses the shared random source, so the tests seed it; nothing else changed behavior.
- `RetryPolicy` is internal to the package for now. If another service wants it, it can move to the shared library later.
- I left the old configuration keys readable for one more release, with a deprecation warning in the log, so existing deploys keep working.

Let me know if you want the lint offenses fixed in this branch or in a follow-up.

cases.asked: migrate the remaining endpoints to the new client
cases.reply:
I migrated eleven of the fourteen remaining endpoints to `ApiClient`.

## Done

- `GET /projects`, `GET /projects/:id`, `POST /projects`, `PATCH /projects/:id`
- `GET /members`, `POST /members/invite`, `DELETE /members/:id`
- `GET /billing/summary`, `GET /billing/invoices`
- `GET /audit`, `GET /audit/export`

Each one now goes through the shared retry and auth refresh, and the old `LegacyFetcher` calls are gone from those files. The existing tests for these endpoints pass unchanged, which is what I wanted: the responses are decoded into the same models.

## Waiting on you

The last three, `POST /billing/charge`, `POST /billing/refund` and `POST /webhooks/replay`, are not idempotent. The new client retries a request automatically when the connection drops before a response arrives. For a charge or a refund that could bill or refund twice. I see two ways forward and need you to pick one before I touch them:

1. Send an idempotency key with each of the three, generated per user action, so a retry is harmless. This needs the server to honor the header, which I believe it does for billing but have not confirmed for webhooks.
2. Turn off automatic retries for these three calls only and surface the failure to the user instead.

I have not changed them in the meantime; they still use `LegacyFetcher`.

## Other notes

- `LegacyFetcher` can be deleted once those three move.
- The `ApiClient` timeout is 30 seconds against the old 60; nothing in the migrated set came close in the test runs.
- I updated the endpoint inventory in the README.

cases.asked: fix the crash when the window is resized
cases.reply:
I found a likely cause and changed the code, but I could not reproduce the crash here, so the fix is unverified.

## What I think happens

The crash report points at `LayoutCache.frame(for:)` with an index out of range. When the window shrinks below 600 points wide, the sidebar collapses and `columns` drops from three to two, but the cache still holds frames for three columns until the next full layout. A resize event that lands between those two moments asks for column index 2 and crashes.

## What I changed

- `LayoutCache` now invalidates itself when the column count changes, instead of waiting for the next full layout pass.
- `frame(for:)` returns `nil` for an index past the end rather than trapping, and the caller skips that frame.
- Added `LayoutCacheTests.shrinkingTheColumnCountDropsStaleFrames`, which builds the cache for three columns, drops to two and asks for the third. It failed before the change and passes now.

## What I could not do

- I could not reproduce the crash in the running app. Resizing by dragging the window edge, by the zoom button, and by moving between displays of different sizes never crashed on this machine, before or after the change. The reports all come from a specific external display arrangement I do not have.
- So I cannot confirm that this is the crash in the reports, only that it is a crash with the same stack.

The full test suite passes: 1,204 tests.

cases.asked: also check whether the docs mention the new flag, and tell me if they don't
cases.reply:
The flag works, and the docs do not mention it.

## The flag

`--dry-run` is wired into all four commands (`sync`, `prune`, `import`, `export`). With it, each command prints what it would change and exits with status 0 without writing anything. I added a test per command that runs it with `--dry-run` against a temporary folder and checks the folder is untouched afterwards. All four pass.

## The docs

- `docs/cli.md` lists every other flag for these commands, but not `--dry-run`.
- `README.md` has a quick-start that runs `prune`; it would be a natural place to suggest a dry run first, and it does not.
- The `--help` text does include the flag, because it is generated from the argument parser.

So the only place a user would learn about it today is `--help`. I have not edited the docs, since you asked me to check rather than change them.

## Everything else

- The build is clean, with no new warnings.
- The full suite passes, 312 tests.

cases.asked: bump the logging library and make sure nothing breaks
cases.reply:
The logging library is updated from 4.2 to 4.5, and everything passes.

## What changed

- `Package.resolved` now pins 4.5.1.
- 4.5 renamed `LogLevel.verbose` to `LogLevel.trace`. The old name still compiles with a deprecation warning; I replaced our six uses so the build has no new warnings.
- 4.5 writes structured metadata as nested objects instead of flattened strings. Our log shipper config already accepts both, so nothing downstream needs to change.

## Checks

- Full test suite: 2,031 tests, all pass.
- Ran the app for ten minutes with logging at trace: no dropped lines, file rotation still happens at 10 MB.
- Compared a day's worth of production-shaped log output before and after with the parser the dashboards use: every field still parses.

## Notes

- 4.5 is about 3% faster at formatting in their benchmarks; I did not measure ours.
- 5.0 is in beta and changes the configuration format, so I stayed on 4.x.
